name: Corteva
description: Since October 1, 2026 Corteva is a pure-play crop protection company: it sells herbicides (48% of FY2025 carve-out net sales of $7.84B), insecticides (21%), fungicides (15%), biologicals (7%) and other products such as nitrogen stabilizers and seed treatments to farmers, distributors and manufacturers, with 37% of sales in North America, 31% in Latin America, 21% in EMEA and 11% in Asia Pacific. Each sale is a one-off product shipment recognized at delivery, net of rebates, discounts and returns, with a smaller stream of sales-based IP licence royalties; sales are seasonal around the planting season. The seed business, Pioneer and the traits, which was 57% of the old company's 2025 sales and about two thirds of its segment profit, was spun off as Vylor (VYLR); Vylor, not Corteva, is the accounting successor of the old Corteva, so the combined history is Vylor's, and Corteva's own record is the carve-out statements filed 2026-10-01. Pro forma for the separation, Corteva had about $3.1B of cash against about $1.0B of debt at 2026-06-30 after receiving about $3.5B in cash from Vylor, and it keeps the legacy EIDP environmental, PFAS and chlorpyrifos exposures. It is being sued by 15 states and one sovereign over the separation.

corporateActions.text: Spun off its seed business as Vylor (VYLR) on Oct 1, 2026, keeping crop protection. Moved from the S&P 500 to the S&P MidCap 400 before the open on Oct 6, 2026. Its financials show as missing until its first report on the new, crop-protection-only basis; the combined history before the spin-off belongs to Vylor.

businessLines.name: Herbicides
businessLines.how: Farmers and distributors buy herbicide products each season; Corteva books the sale at shipment net of rebates, discounts and returns. The filings attribute the price declines of 2024, 2025 and the first half of 2026 mainly to the competitive pricing environment in Latin America, offset by volume from new products.

brands.note: Wholly owned operating subsidiary of Corteva, Inc. and a separate SEC reporting issuer; its $3.50 and $4.50 Series Preferred Stock (NYSE: CTAPrA, CTAPrB) stay outstanding with third-party holders and are shown as noncontrolling interests ($239M at 2026-06-30). EIDP's seed-side subsidiary Pioneer Hi-Bred International went to Vylor.

geography.method: Regional revenue tagged in the filing's own XBRL instance: full-year contexts with one geographic dimension (or segments named after places), alone or crossed only with operating segments or a revenue line of the income statement; regions must add up to the revenue line within 1 percent; a member equal to the sum of others is a subtotal; the main split is the largest set of members adding up to the total; anything not broken out is a computed remainder.
